components.name: Topology node
components.description: Native rounded rectangle; fill color records its topology category.
components.css: .ds-topology-node { display: inline-block; border: 1.4px solid #263848; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 12px; color: #233647; background: #ffffff; font-family: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.25; } .ds-topology-node--physical { background: #e7eff8; } .ds-topology-node--guest { background: #e8f4f0; } .ds-topology-node--logical { background: #f0edf9; } .ds-topology-node--service { background: #ffffff; } .ds-topology-node--device { background: #fff3df; }

components.name: Frame title
components.description: Native text heading anchored at the upper-left of an Excalidraw frame.

components.name: Flow annotation
components.description: Teal label paired with a native directional flow connector.
components.css: .ds-flow-label { color: #2c7185; font-family: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; }

narrative.overview:
One native Excalidraw scene combines the 131-node, 130-edge ownership and network-attachment tree with 20 labelled flow frames. The tree shows physical devices and hosts through VM/LXC guests to Docker and Kubernetes services. Focused frames trace selected request and data paths.

The public scene is names-only. The private scene adds IP:port labels from local ignored address maps. The scene uses native shapes, text, frames and arrows; its PNGs are frame exports. Local rendering uses the official CLI and needs no account, API key or hosted service.
keyCharacteristics: One editable canvas: a left-to-right topology tree and 20 focused flow frames.
Node fill identifies physical, guest, logical, service or device categories.
Relationship labels carry meaning; connector styling alone is not a relationship taxonomy.

rules.name: The Labelled-Arrow Rule
rules.body: Read the arrow label for relationship meaning. Do not infer packet flow, membership or dependency from color or dash style alone.

dos: Do use the tree for ownership and network attachment, and flow frames for labelled end-to-end paths.
Do read each relationship label, especially on dashed fan-out connectors.
Do preserve unknown hardware and network details as unknown.
Do keep the IP-bearing scene and address sources private.
donts: Don't read every tree edge as a packet path.
Don't infer relationship semantics from dash style or color alone.
Don't publish the private scene or its local address maps.
